_source: README Expected outcomes — E2E-02, minus the info-count assertion. The `"info": { "min": 1 }` rule was REMOVED after two E2E gate runs 20 minutes apart, on identical code, disagreed: run A passed, run B reported `info findings 0 below min 1`. Whether an info-level nit surfaces at all is model judgement, and the `correctness` tag means a DETERMINISTIC contract — so that one rule did not belong under it. Everything below is mechanical and still asserted: a clean PR renders the all-clear shape, scores 5, and approves. If the info note becomes deterministic, restore the rule rather than loosening anything else. mergewatch.ai#626: the clean-verdict wording changed from "All clear! No issues found — this PR looks good to go" to "Looks good to me! I didn't find anything worth raising in this diff". The old text asserted ABSENCE the review never verified (nothing checks that silence was right) and appended a merge recommendation covering tests and CI that MergeWatch never reads. The new phrasing is a first-person judgement, which is what the product is actually entitled to say — it already submits a formal APPROVE at 4-5.
